structureNote: Printed hierarchy: Skill (1.0 Listening / 2.0 Speaking / 3.0 Reading / 4.0 Writing / 5.0 Literature in Action) > Content Standard (e.g. 1.1) with FOCUS statements > Learning Standard (e.g. 1.1.1). The printed DSKP has no per-topic unit hierarchy: each 'unit' here is one skill per form (5 per level). 'sk' = Content Standard code/title, 'sp' = Learning Standards (some printed as 'No learning standard'). 'focus' lists the FOCUS column statements (they are not mapped 1:1 to codes in the printed table). 'tahapPenguasaan' = the six Performance Levels of the Performance Standards Guide for that skill (Literature in Action has none: assessed through the four skills). Themes and topics are only named at syllabus level (themes below) and detailed in the separate Scheme of Work, not in this document. Target proficiency: CEFR B1 Mid by end of Form 4.

newGrammar: Broader range of intensifiers (too, so, such)
Used to and would (for past habits, routines and states)
Be able to/ can/ manage to
I wish (Wish + Past Simple - Regrets about now)
Zero, First and Second Conditional (unless in first conditional)
Reported speech (requests / reporting verbs and their various patterns: agree to, remind someone to, suggest that, accuse of, deny + ing, refuse to)
mainLanguageFunctions: Connecting words expressing a contrast: although, even though, however, in case, despite, in spite of
Connecting words expressing cause: because, because of, as a result of, due to
Connecting words expressing an effect: so, consequently, as a result, thus, therefore
Wh- questions in the present and past
Indirect questions with know, wonder etc.
Asking for help / offering advice (Would you mind/like + -ing?)

newGrammar: Future simple (using shall); future perfect simple; future perfect continuous; temporals (using: when, before, after, until, etc.)
mainLanguageFunctions: Modals, such as for requests, offers and suggestions, necessity, deduction, advice, criticism
The passive: impersonal and personal structures
Explaining effects using determining verbs (caused, led to)
Making comparisons to explain opinion (for time using in the old days, in the past, nowadays, now)
Connecting words expressing a contrast (using: although, however, on the other hand)
Using conditional sentences to explain reasons
Phrases to show opinion (for example: in my opinion)
